description: An automated system to track weekly changes in Canvas courses by downloading IMSCC exports, comparing them against previous versions, and emailing an interactive HTML diff report to stakeholders.

modules.name: Controller (main.py)
modules.description: Reads the configuration, delegates tasks to workers sequentially, and handles overall error logging and task flow.

modules.name: Configuration Manager (config_loader.py)
modules.description: Loads the JSON database of Canvas course links, email lists, and app settings.

modules.name: Canvas Scraper (scraper.py)
modules.description: Uses Playwright or Selenium to authenticate to Canvas, navigate to course settings, trigger content export, and download the IMSCC file to a designated staging directory.

modules.name: IMSCC Processor (imscc_handler.py)
modules.description: Extracts the downloaded IMSCC (ZIP format) files into course-specific and timestamp-specific directories.

modules.name: Diff Generator (differ.py)
modules.description: Compares the current week's extracted files against the previous week's files. Generates a structured dictionary containing categorized diffs (Assignments, Pages, Settings, etc.) and semantic tags (Content Changes, Grading Rules, Dates).

modules.name: HTML Reporter (html_reporter.py)
modules.description: Consumes the data from differ.py to generate a beautiful, interactive HTML presentation. Includes a Dashboard tab and a Raw Logs tab. The logs feature collapsible categories and individual files, with a toggle to switch between a rich Canvas-like rendered view and a raw code diff view.

modules.name: Email Notifier (emailer.py)
modules.description: Reads the generated HTML report and emails it as an attachment to the configured list of shareholders using SMTP or an email API, providing a summary in the email body.

modules.name: Task Scheduler Setup (scheduler_setup.ps1)
modules.description: A PowerShell script to configure Windows Task Scheduler to run the Controller script upon the first user logon of the week.

agentInstructions: Integrate the Gemini API to analyze the full page context alongside the raw diff to generate human-readable descriptions of the changes.
Ensure strict modularity. Each worker must have clear input and output interfaces and should not depend tightly on other workers.
Use robust error handling for the web scraping module, as Canvas UI might be slow or change slightly.
The IMSCC (which is a ZIP format) extraction should handle large files safely.
The diff generation should compare file hashes and structures. For text-based files (XML/HTML), generate line-by-line diffs if modified.

The diff generation should categorize changes by Canvas component (Pages, Quizzes, Assignments) and append semantic labels (e.g., [Content Change], [Grading Rule], [Date/Restriction]) based on keywords in the diff lines for future data analysis.
The system must track the consecutive number of weeks a course has had zero changes via persistent state.

If a course has had zero changes for 5 or more consecutive weeks, the HTML report must display a prominent recommendation for the designer to check standard pages/resources to help maintain the course.
All configuration (URLs, emails, credentials, API keys) must be read from environment variables or a secure local configuration file.

expectedBehaviors.trigger: Executes on Windows Logon. The main script includes wrapper logic that ensures the heavy lifting only runs if it hasn't run successfully yet for the current calendar week.
expectedBehaviors.processing: Iterates through all courses sequentially, downloading and unzipping their IMSCC.
expectedBehaviors.comparison: Finds the immediate previous export folder for each course. If none exists, treats all files as 'new'. Otherwise, runs a recursive directory diff.
expectedBehaviors.reporting: Consolidates all course diffs into a single interactive HTML document with collapsible tabs, semantic labeling, and rich rendering of additions/deletions.
expectedBehaviors.delivery: Sends the HTML document as an email attachment (to bypass email client JS restrictions) to the shareholder list.
